title: Initial-Condition Variability in Elementary Cellular Automata: Local-Descriptor Prediction and an Exploratory Density Association
content: Elementary cellular automata (ECA) are deterministic systems whose global behavior depends on both local update rules and initial states. While local rules are simple, predicting global variability remains a challenge. Here, we quantify this variation across all 256 Wolfram rules using 100 independent random initial states per rule (width 200, 200 updates) and test whether local rule-table descriptors predict the variance. Using mean normalized LZ78 complexity as the trajectory-level outcome, we define the rule-level target as the standard deviation of this score across seeds. Under five-fold cross-validation grouped by symmetry equivalence classes, an enriched ridge model yielded an  of 0.0157, demonstrating that local descriptors provide weak predictive performance for global variance. In an exploratory extension, we fit Gaussian mixtures to the LZ scores of ten previously selected rules. Across two lattice widths, held-out trajectories assigned to high- and low-complexity components exhibited repeatable differences in mean density, though a secondary damage-spreading measure showed no significant effects. These results characterize finite-size outcome variability and highlight a repeatable association between LZ-based complexity and density, without establishing distinct dynamical regimes or absolute limits on local prediction.
